notes: Under-the-hood work, no visible changes. Three things got safer or faster. Saving is now crash-proof: chores, the wiki, recipes, countdowns and the message board used to be written straight over the live file, so losing power partway through a save could leave the file unreadable and the hub would quietly start over with an empty one. Every save now writes to the side and swaps in the finished copy, so a bad moment can't cost you the chore board. The hub is also about 30% quicker to answer each request — it was re-reading its accounts and sign-in files from disk on every single one, including every camera thumbnail on the dashboard — and it now asks Home Assistant once when several screens want the same thing at the same moment, instead of once per screen. Finally, the offline mode had fallen eight pages behind: Recipes, Stack Health, Manage, Internet Access and Countdowns never worked without a connection. They do now, and the list keeps itself up to date from here on.
